notes: Hardware-verified as an Apollo x6 by physical inspection: 2 mic preamps, 6 analog I/O total. Observed serial '2048 2019 011389' — serial_prefix is digits 5-8 (the group ua_read_serial_type() matches), serial_leading is digits 1-4. IMPORTANT: device_type here is 0x1E (UA_DEV_APOLLO_X6), which is correct but is NOT what the driver currently reports. ua_detect_capabilities() pins device_type = 0x20 (x8p) for any device with PCI subsystem 0x0014 (ua_core.c:214-221), so the daemon will not match this descriptor until detection is fixed. Two independent bugs both resolve this unit as x8p: the subsystem pin, and ua_serial_table's '2019' entry (ua_core.c:250), which maps to UA_DEV_APOLLO_X8P and is wrong — 2019 is x6, verified against hardware here. Fixing either alone leaves the misdetection in place. subsystem_id 0x0014 is a PLATFORM id, not a model id. This x6 is indistinguishable from the device devices/apollo-x8p.json describes on every signal except the serial: PCI subsystem (0x0014), FPGA revision (0xa241c5ac), DSP count (6), the name string at 0xC034 ('Apollo'), and all 86 entries of both IO descriptors are identical. Only the serial differs (2019 here vs 2017 there). Do not identify a model by subsystem ID on this platform. The serial reads 0xff on a cold device and only populates after ACEFACE connect, which is why the probe-time lookup fails; post-connect the whole low register block appears (FW_VERSION 0x03001c00, HW_UID_LO 0x36094470). channels are the DMA fabric counts the hardware reports and the driver programs (34 play / 32 rec @ 48kHz), NOT analog jack counts. They reconcile with the IO descriptors: input 34 minus S/PDIF(2) = 32 record; output 52 minus S/PDIF(2) minus the 16 unnamed group 0x0c entries = 34 playback. Those descriptors are a platform constant — this x6 reports LINE 5-8 inputs and LINE 1-8 outputs for which it has no connectors, so they cannot be used to derive analog fitment or preamp count. preamps is the physical count (2). The driver exposes 8 preamp strips because ua_models[] carries preamps=8 for device_type 0x20 (ua_audio.c:95). hiz is UNVERIFIED: the platform input descriptor lists channels 1-2 as MIC/LINE/HIZ, but that descriptor overstates analog fitment as noted above. features are taken from the clock-source table the device publishes at BAR0+0xC090 (S/PDIF, ADAT, Word Clock, Peer2Peer, Internal; readable cold, no driver needed). None are physically verified on this unit, and the table may itself be a platform constant rather than per-SKU — treat as unconfirmed. Note Word Clock is absent from the x8p descriptor's feature list. STATUS: AUDIO CONFIRMED BOTH DIRECTIONS. Playback verified audibly — PipeWire auto-configured the raw node as default sink and mapped stereo FL/FR to playback_AUX0/AUX1, which the output IO descriptor identifies as MON L/R, so system audio reaches the monitor outputs with NO PipeWire/UCM/WirePlumber configs deployed (configs/deploy.sh was never run). Capture verified by loopback: a -12 dBFS 440 Hz tone played to the monitor outs while recording all 32 capture channels appeared on capture AUX26/AUX27 at -8.2 dBFS peak, 99.9% non-zero, with the other 30 channels at exact digital zero. Channel identity for that pair is unconfirmed: the input descriptor has 34 entries against 32 ALSA channels, so two are dropped — if S/PDIF (dma[16..17]) is the dropped pair, as ua_routing.h states, AUX26/27 is AUX1 L/R; under a straight truncation it is MON L/R. No routing table was sent (dmesg shows the IO descriptors read but never written), so channel order is the FPGA default. The two mic preamp channels (capture AUX0/AUX1) read exact digital zero rather than self-noise — consistent with nothing routed to them rather than merely no signal present; the reference device reportedly showed -102/-106 dBFS self-noise there. 48kHz only — the driver advertises no other rate. Tested on a WARM device (driver logged 'mixer DSP alive! Skipping DMA reset to preserve state'); cold behaviour unverified. Host: Apple iMac18,3, Alpine Ridge JHL6540 TB3, kernel 6.8.0-139-generic. Full analysis in FINDINGS-apollo-x6.md.
